key_insight: El Agente Quntur is a conversational research agent that democratizes quantum chemistry by orchestrating simulation tools and translating results into actionable chemical insight, enabling non-experts to run and interpret quantum calculations.
problem_solved: Removes the expert-only barrier to quantum chemistry caused by methodological complexity, heterogeneous software stacks, and the need for informed interpretation of numerical outputs.
method: Agent architecture that couples a language model with domain-specific tool connectors (quantum chemistry packages, parsers, job managers) to plan and execute simulations.
Automated workflow orchestration: selects methods/basis sets, submits and monitors calculations, parses outputs, and performs error handling and retries.
Interactive interpretation layer that converts numerical results into plain-language summaries, visualizations, and next-step experiment or computation suggestions with expert-in-the-loop validation.
impact: Makes quantum-chemistry workflows accessible to ML/AI practitioners and experimental chemists, enabling rapid dataset generation, reproducible simulation pipelines, and integration of domain-aware agents into automated discovery loops.
visual_elements: System architecture diagram: LLM agent ↔ QC toolchain (connectors, job scheduler, parsers) ↔ user interface
Flowchart of a typical session: user query → plan → run calculation → parse results → interpret & recommend
Before/after comparison panel: required expertise/time vs. democratized workflow/time saved
Example results card: molecular structure, key computed properties (energies, spectra), and concise plain-language explanation
paper_title: El Agente Quntur: A research collaborator agent for quantum chemistry
paper_authors: Juan B. Pérez-Sánchez, Yunheng Zou, Jorge A. Campos-Gonzalez-Angulo, Marcel Müller, Ignacio Gustin
